chunks: From him, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayyub ibn Nuha, from Safwan, from Sayf al-Tammari, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'A man from your mawali makes the girdles (hamail) with pig hair.' He said, 'When he finishes, let him wash his hand.'

key_terms.الْحَمَائِلَ: Girdles or belts, plural of حَمِيل

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing hands after working with pig hair in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from the chapter on earnings (Al-Makasib) illustrates the practical application of ritual purity in commercial crafts, specifically addressing the use of pig hair for girdles. Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) prescribes washing the hand after completion, indicating that while the material is impure, the act of working with it does not render the worker permanently impure, provided the immediate contact is cleansed. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view on the transfer of najāsah through direct contact in trade.
